workedExample.title: M20 Mix for 10 m³ Slab Example
workedExample.scenario: 10 m³ of M20 concrete (1:1.5:3 ratio). Dry volume = 10 × 1.54 = 15.4 m³.

faqs.question: Why multiply concrete wet volume by 1.54?
faqs.answer: Dry sand and gravel contain air voids between particles; when mixed with water, the volume shrinks by ~35%, so 1.54 dry volume produces 1.0 wet volume.

faqs.question: What is the standard water-cement ratio for M20?
faqs.answer: A water-cement ratio of 0.45 to 0.50 (approx. 25-28 liters per 50 kg cement bag) is standard.

en.notes: Multiplies wet concrete volume by 1.54 dry factor to compensate for voids, then apportions by nominal mix ratio.

faqs.question: セメント1袋（50kg）に対する標準水量は？
